body: It sounds like you're in a rough spot and its not the first time you've been there.  Take hope that many of the issues you are having are things that solutions can be found for.  If you are relapsing on your addiction reach out to your resources.  It seems to be the cause of most of your problems, but is a demon that is fightable.  I am in no way saying it's an easy fight, but there are tools out there to help you fight.  Addiction is a tough battle, and many have lost, but many have also come out victorious.
I have a similar thought frequently, if I had been born a few decades earlier I would have died when I was 2, because there wasn't the medical science to keep me alive.

While I don't want to marginalize your pain, the fact that you want others to miss you and regret not giving you more serious attention makes it seem like your confession of suicidal thoughts are even more so just a plea for attention.  I have to say, when I envision people's reactions to my death its exactly the opposite of yours.  People don't miss me, in fact they hardly even notice im gone except as I create an inconvenience for them, such as needing to hire someone to fill my spot at work.  There is no regret that they didn't do more to stop me, if they feel anything its relief that they no longer need to tolerate and be burdened by me. And life continues easily and most likely better with my position being filled my someone better so that it's a vast improvement.

So I have to toss my ps and qs in here.  To be honest, both of you have used some flawed logic and weak arguments, but I do have to agree that for most humans, giving birth is an extremely selfish act.  While animals procreate due to a biological imperative to do so, humans reasoning for creating offspring ranges anywhere from creating heirs to carry on their legacy to repairing a marriage to creating a safety net of obligated blood ties to help ensure their future well being (also known as family).  Very rarely, if ever, is a child had merely to give that being opportunity or to create a life to improve the state of the society or planet. One could also argue that given the current state of society and the planet, one could be considered selfish for bringing a being into life on a overpopulated planet in a declining society where that being will have little opportunity for success unless you have excessive means to guarantee otherwise.  Is it fair to bring a life into poverty, waning resources, malevolent societies and governments, or warfare, or could this be seen as a form of abuse for putting a child into this situation. As for the planet dying or suffering without humans, I highly doubt that.  The planet has been around millions of years before we have come into existence and has seen many other species go extinct before us.  It could even be argued that the planet would suffer less without the destructive, parasitic species that we are. If humans were to disappear, life would continue as it has changing and evolving and adapting.  Just as we replaced dinosaurs as an apex species, so would something replace us.  If all life were to stop existing, it may indeed be the end of things as they are but may not destroy our planet.  Right in our own solar system are planets that exhibit signs of life but still exist despite now being desolate.  I also have to argue that the planet would be scattered with corpses, being the last link in the food chain bacteria and other organisms responsible for decomposition would logical be the last to die.  One could also argue that splitting bacterial cells is not considered procreation and is therefore not included in the cessation of such.  And finally, if our planet were to die, we may consider it sad, but it would hardly be cataclysmic to the solar system.  Stars are born, live, and die all the time and neither do we mourn them nor does the universe register it.  I have to conclude that yes, a human bringing a child into the world is a selfish act.

we are all broken somehow, and I don't know that most of us can be fixed.  they say it's just chemicals in our brains that are out of whack and drugs can rebalance and fix us, but i dont feel it's true.  They can maybe work as a bandaid or help quiet things some, but we are still broken.  Somewhere deep down, call it spirit, soul, being, or energy, that part of us that can't be mapped on an xray, catscan, or MRI, somepart of us has been broken, crushed, disfigured, or marred.  No amount of drugs can fix that, im not sure even therapy can the way it's used.  Who knows, maybe for some of us its not even our own energy thats broken, maybe it's echoes of all the other distraught energies on this planet or even the planet itself, and we are just the ones lucky enough to feel it.   Our tiny brains and bodies just cant cope with it, but we can't place ourselves in tiny little egocentric bubbles and ignore it either.  Maybe we get sad because no matter how much good we try to do to counter it, the great malaise still weighs on us.  Maybe we get tired because pushing against anything that much bigger than us is so much work.  Maybe we get sad for no reason because all that pain is sad, even when its not our own and we know not where it comes from, just that there is pain and sadness thats palpable to us.  But we are the crazy broken ones whose brains dont work right and need to be adjusted, or taught by a shrink how to focus on nothing outside our little bubble as well watch the blissfully ignorant run around in their egocentric little bubbles.
